summary.text: The Last Glacial Maximum was the most recent time in the Last Glacial Period when ice sheets were at their greatest extent, between 26,000 and 20,000 years ago.
Ice sheets covered much of northern North America, northern Europe and Asia, causing deserts to spread widely and sea levels to drop sharply.
With so much water locked in ice, sea level sat about 125 meters lower than today, exposing continental shelves and joining land masses together.

facts.label: Atmospheric dust
facts.value: Up to 20 to 25 times today's levels

items.prompt: During the Last Glacial Maximum, coastlines lay far out from where they are now. Where had the missing seawater gone?

options.label: It evaporated into a much wetter atmosphere
It drained into caves under the sea floor
It was locked up in massive ice sheets
It was trapped in huge inland lakes

items.explain: The ice sheets locked away water, which lowered sea level and exposed continental shelves.

items.prompt: Parts of Siberia were about as cold as ice-covered Europe, yet no big ice sheets grew there. Why not?

options.label: The ground was too warm from below
The air was too dry to drop enough snow
Strong sunlight melted the ice each summer
The land was too flat for ice to collect

items.explain: Ice sheets need both lasting cold and snowfall; air reaching Siberia was so dry that enough snow for glaciers never fell.

items.prompt: Ice cores show the air was far dustier at the Last Glacial Maximum. What best explains that?

options.label: Less plant cover, stronger winds and less rain
A long series of meteor impacts
Smoke from early human campfires
Ice sheets grinding rock into the sea

items.explain: Reduced vegetation, stronger global winds and less rain to wash dust out of the air probably all played a part.

items.prompt: Compared with today, how did rainfall and temperature change across most of the world at the Last Glacial Maximum?

options.label: Cooler and much wetter almost everywhere
Cooler, with rainfall unchanged
Warmer and drier in most places
Cooler and drier almost everywhere

items.explain: Climates were cooler and almost everywhere drier, as the water cycle slowed down.

items.prompt: The ice sheets made the northern Pacific and Atlantic cool and form more clouds. What did those extra clouds do to the global chill?

options.label: Eased it by trapping heat near the ground
Had no effect on temperature
Strengthened it by reflecting more sunlight
Ended it by bringing warm rain north

items.explain: The clouds reflected even more sunlight, amplifying the global cooling.

items.prompt: While most of the world's deserts grew, something different happened in what is now desert in the western United States. What?

options.label: It froze under a thick ice sheet
It turned into shifting sand dunes
It sank below sea level
Heavy rain filled large lakes there

items.explain: Changes in the jet stream brought heavy rain, forming large lakes such as Lake Bonneville in Utah.
